title: Make the agent role registry configurable instead of hardcoded
description: Make the agent role registry configurable instead of hardcoded

newDescription: Right now, the Decision Engine's agent roles (Architect, Backend Developer, Security Reviewer, Release Manager, Performance Reviewer, Domain Expert) are hardcoded Java constants in Roles.java -- adding, removing, or changing a role's mandate requires recompiling the engine. docs/high-level-architecture.md already commits to this being wrong long-term: 'The platform must be able to register new agent types -- including via plugins -- without changing the core architecture. The role registry, not the model, defines what an agent is allowed to do and decide.' There is a stated preference for a shared YAML config file to define the role registry instead. There is also interest in a RACI-matrix structure -- docs/design/decision-making.md already frames the category-to-owner table as RACI's 'Accountable,' so the config format should be able to express Responsible/Accountable/Consulted/Informed per category, not just a flat list of role names and mandates. Propose a concrete approach: where the config file lives, its schema (role name, mandate text, and RACI-style category assignments), whether RACI needs to be captured now or can be added later without a breaking format change, and how the current six hardcoded roles migrate into it without breaking anything already using them.
